From a matter of fact standpoint - this is where we are:

- Anthropic IPO price being marked down on public markets, OpenAI slashing the amount they're raising 

- Companies have had multiple quarters to show AI growth, which just isn't coming out at the same rate that the market expects them to be

- We are seeing the wave of adoption come from bad actors with many hacks / breaches - and as humans, negativity bias is real and more and more people are seeing AI for how it's being used for evil and not good - which usually takes far longer to produce

- Individual AI stocks down anywhere from 10 - 30% from ATHs, with markedly more volatility from before ; more volatility after a large run up usually comes from the end of the cycle

- Most Americans are reporting more and more "economic uncertainty" - and they are less optimistic about the economic reality of their future

- Rising costs of living and inflation and gas costs are genuinely being felt by people on the ground

- After months of uncertainty, this is finally being baked into prices somewhat; indexes across the world are already down anywhere from 10 - 30% ; 

Two things can be true - AI can be early in terms of adoption and how it's being used, but prices in the markets can also be far overshot in reality. 

It is also clear that price IS moving downwards and there is just a huge wave of anger amongst semis participants about why their stocks should be at the highs

Today we’re releasing GDPx, a benchmark for measuring agentic capabilities across the most valuable domains.

GDPx is a true frontier-level benchmark: even the best model scores just 12% (1/7)🧵 https://t.co/RNnkcuUkih

We believe the first trillion dollars of AI revenue will be concentrated in sectors that can deploy frontier intelligence at high ROI, not broadly diffused throughout the whole economy. Building a general-purpose benchmark based on share of GDP or the SOC/O*NET occupational taxonomy is therefore a mistake. If your goal is to track the progress of frontier models, you should focus on the domains where they will be most impactful. This is why we include chip design, cyber, and bio over domains like government, real estate, and insurance. (3/7)

GDPx covers the following domains. Each was a collaboration with at least one specialized data partner. SemiAnalysis was responsible for final QA and heavily involved with task iteration. (2/7) https://t.co/V2jywe3L1o

We believe it’s underrated how relevant safety classifiers are when picking the best model for certain use cases. For example, Muse Wonder Full is actually the best available cyber model today by a meaningful margin. (5/7) https://t.co/l8Kg3o5uTR

It’s worth emphasizing that certain models like Opus 5.5 and GPT-6 Astra have sandbagged overall scores due to their safety classifiers. If we exclude cyber, biology, and alignment—the three domains where safety classifiers sometimes kick in—you get the following results instead.

We were pleasantly surprised by how well this ranking lines up with our subjective impression of the models. (4/7)
